name: Sago Palm / Cycads
description: Sago Palm (Cycas revoluta) and other cycads are extremely dangerous and highly toxic to cats. Every single part of the plant—leaves, trunk, and roots—is poisonous, but the seeds (or "nuts") contain the highest concentration of toxins and are the most deadly part. Ingesting just one or two seeds can be fatal. The main toxin, cycasin, causes severe and rapid liver failure. When a cat eats any part of the plant, the toxin is absorbed and begins to destroy liver cells. This damage is often irreversible and happens very quickly. The plant also contains other toxins that affect the nervous system. Symptoms of Sago Palm poisoning can appear within hours and include vomiting (sometimes with blood), diarrhea, drooling, weakness, and loss of appetite. As the liver fails, you may see yellowing of the skin and eyes (jaundice), seizures, and bleeding. Any suspected ingestion is a life-threatening emergency. Please contact a veterinarian or an emergency animal hospital immediately.
safetyNotes: Toxic compounds: cycasin (methylazoxymethanol glycoside) in all parts; seeds contain the highest concentration
Mechanism: cycasin is metabolised to methylazoxymethanol (MAM), a powerful alkylating agent causing hepatocellular necrosis and DNA cross-linking
Symptoms (within 15 minutes to 3 hours): vomiting, diarrhea, drooling, lethargy; severe liver failure follows: jaundice, bleeding, neurological signs, coma
Seeds are the greatest risk — 1–2 seeds can kill a cat; all parts carry life-threatening toxicity
Any suspected ingestion is a critical veterinary emergency — survival depends on immediate, aggressive treatment

symptoms.name: Vomiting, drooling, anorexia, severe abdominal pain, increased thirst, and diarrhea (which may be bloody or appear as black, "tarry" feces)
symptoms.onset: Initial clinical signs typically appear rapidly, often within the first 4 hours of ingestion
symptoms.notes: These initial stomach and intestinal symptoms act as an early indicator of poisoning before the plant's toxins begin destroying the internal organs.

symptoms.name: Jaundice (yellowing of the skin and eyes), profound hepatic necrosis, and severe liver failure
symptoms.onset: Progresses over 48 to 72 hours following ingestion
symptoms.notes: This is caused by cycasin, a highly toxic compound in the plant that is broken down in the gut into methylazoxymethanol, which aggressively attacks the liver37. Ingesting as little as 1 to 2 seeds can cause fatal liver failure.

symptoms.name: Bruising, blood clots, petechiae (pinpoint spots of bleeding), ecchymotic hemorrhages, and generalized abnormal bleeding
symptoms.onset: Delayed; develops secondary to liver failure within 48 to 72 hours
symptoms.notes: As the liver tissue dies (hepatic necrosis), it loses its ability to produce essential clotting factors, leading to life-threatening secondary bleeding disorders throughout the body.

symptoms.name: Lethargy, extreme weakness, ataxia (loss of coordination), tremors, paralysis, seizures, coma, and eventually death
symptoms.notes: These neurological symptoms are caused both directly by the plant's neurotoxin (beta-methylamino-L-alanine, or BMAA) and indirectly as a consequence of the liver shutting down.

scientificName: Cycas revoluta, Cycas cirinalis, Zamia spp.
